Rule_Name: Total Storage Requirement Must Include All Required Data Objects
What_It_Means: Required storage capacity shall include the workload's concurrently or persistently required dataset copies, model files, checkpoints, temporary files and explicitly retained logs/cache.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: dataset size; model size; checkpoint retention; temporary workspace; logs/cache
Condition: All listed storage objects are required
Output_Decision: Calculate total required usable storage before applying WLR-STOR-01.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: All listed storage objects are required = Workload-derived GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel
Limitations: Do not count temporary objects that are never concurrently/persistently required; deduplicate identical copies.
Applicability: Training and inference deployments with persistent data artifacts.
Example_or_Context: Training and inference deployments with persistent data artifacts.

Rule_Name: Training Dataset Capacity Must Preserve Required Dataset Representation
What_It_Means: Training storage sizing shall use the actual retained dataset representation and any required replicas/shards/staging copies rather than assuming nominal source size alone.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: dataset bytes; format; compression; replicas; shards
Condition: Training dataset is retained on storage
Output_Decision: Produce training dataset storage component.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Training dataset is retained on storage = Measured/configured GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / MLPerf Storage v1.0 Benchmark Results
Limitations: Raw dataset size and transformed/cache representations can differ.

Rule_Name: Inference Dataset Capacity Must Be Modeled Separately
What_It_Means: Inference datasets, evaluation sets, reference corpora or retrieval data shall be sized according to their actual retained storage footprint; training-dataset assumptions must not be reused automatically.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: inference dataset size; replicas; index/reference files
Output_Decision: Produce inference dataset storage component.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Inference data is persistently stored = Measured/configured GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results
Limitations: Online inference may use object/shared storage rather than local copies.
Applicability: Batch/online inference with stored input/reference data.
Example_or_Context: Batch/online inference with stored input/reference data.

Rule_Name: Model Files Must Be Included in Storage Capacity
What_It_Means: Model weights, tokenizer/configuration files and required model artifacts shall be included when retained by the deployment.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: model file sizes; number of model versions; format
Output_Decision: Add retained model artifact footprint.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Model artifacts are retained = Measured/configured GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel
Limitations: GPU memory size is not a substitute for persistent model-file size.

Rule_Name: Checkpoint Capacity Must Reflect Retention Policy
What_It_Means: Checkpoint storage shall account for checkpoint size, checkpoint frequency and retention policy. Distributed/sharded checkpoint layouts shall use their actual written data volume.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: checkpoint size; frequency; retention count; sharding
Output_Decision: Calculate persistent checkpoint capacity.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Checkpointing enabled = Configured GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel / New MLPerf Storage v2.0 Benchmark Results
Limitations: Checkpoint logical model state and actual on-disk footprint can differ due to format/metadata/sharding.

Rule_Name: Temporary Workspace Must Be Included When Peak Disk Usage Requires It
What_It_Means: Temporary preprocessing files, intermediate artifacts, extraction/transform outputs and other disk-resident scratch data shall be included when they can coexist with required persistent data.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: peak temporary workspace; overlap timing
Output_Decision: Add peak concurrent temporary storage requirement.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Temporary disk objects are created = Measured/configured GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / MLPerf Storage v1.0 Benchmark Results
Limitations: Do not use cumulative lifetime writes as capacity requirement; use peak resident disk occupancy.
Applicability: Preprocessing and training pipelines with disk intermediates.
Example_or_Context: Preprocessing and training pipelines with disk intermediates.

Rule_Name: Logs and Persistent Cache Must Be Included When Retained
What_It_Means: Logs, metadata, indexes and persistent caches shall be included only when their retention period or configured size makes them part of the required storage footprint.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: log growth; retention; cache size
Output_Decision: Add retained logs/cache capacity.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Logs/cache are retained = Configured/Measured GB/TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results
Limitations: Ephemeral logs and automatically evicted caches may not require full persistent capacity.

Rule_Name: Required Read Throughput Must Be Derived From Workload Data Consumption
What_It_Means: Required storage read throughput shall be derived from the workload's actual data-consumption pattern and target processing rate, not from a universal GB/s threshold.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: data consumed per unit; target samples/batches/requests per second
Condition: Storage must sustain the workload data stream
Output_Decision: Produce required read-throughput target for WLR-STOR-02.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Storage must sustain the workload data stream = Workload-derived GB/s or MB/s
Source_Title: GPUDirect Storage Benchmarking and Configuration Guide / MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / MLPerf Storage v1.0 Benchmark Results
Limitations: Caching, compression and direct I/O can change physical storage demand.

Rule_Name: Required Write Throughput Must Be Derived From Write Workload
What_It_Means: Required storage write throughput shall be derived from checkpointing, preprocessing outputs, logs or other write streams that must meet a time objective.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: bytes to write; allowed write window
Condition: A write operation has a target completion time
Output_Decision: Produce required write-throughput target.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: A write operation has a target completion time = Workload-derived GB/s
Source_Title: GPUDirect Storage Benchmarking and Configuration Guide / MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / New MLPerf Storage v2.0 Benchmark Results
Limitations: No universal write bandwidth threshold; durability semantics can affect elapsed time.

Rule_Name: Small-I/O Workloads Must Be Characterized Using IOPS and Latency
What_It_Means: When storage requests are small or metadata/file-operation intensive, DSS shall evaluate IOPS and latency in addition to aggregate throughput.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: IO size; operation rate; latency
Output_Decision: Use IOPS/latency constraints instead of relying only on GB/s.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Small/random/metadata I/O dominates = Workload-dependent IOPS; ms/us
Source_Title: GPUDirect Storage Benchmarking and Configuration Guide / MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results
Limitations: No universal IO-size cutoff is imposed; workload benchmark determines relevance.

Rule_Name: Sequential I/O Must Be Evaluated Separately From Random I/O
What_It_Means: Storage evaluation shall preserve whether the workload is sequential or random because the access pattern affects which performance metric is meaningful.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: request size; access pattern; read/write mix
Output_Decision: Select appropriate throughput/IOPS/latency measurements.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Access pattern is known = Sequential/Random/Mixed
Source_Title: GPUDirect Storage Benchmarking and Configuration Guide
Limitations: Mixed workloads require representative proportions rather than a single synthetic pattern.

Rule_Name: Storage Latency Must Be Evaluated When It Can Stall the Pipeline
What_It_Means: Storage latency shall be included when individual I/O completion time can delay data availability, checkpoint completion, request service or recovery.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: I/O latency; pipeline wait; SLA/recovery objective
Condition: Latency affects workload completion or data availability
Output_Decision: Include latency requirement or diagnostic metric.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Latency affects workload completion or data availability = Workload-dependent ms/us
Source_Title: GPUDirect Storage Benchmarking and Configuration Guide / MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results
Limitations: No universal latency threshold; use workload/service objective.

Rule_Name: Storage-to-CPU-to-GPU Path Must Be Modeled When Storage Does Not Directly Feed GPU
What_It_Means: When the application uses storage→CPU/host memory→GPU movement, the storage requirement shall be evaluated at the storage stage and compared with the downstream consumption rate.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: storage read rate; CPU staging; GPU consumption rate; buffering
Output_Decision: Identify storage as a potential producer bottleneck before GPU consumption.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: CPU staging path is used = Path-dependent GB/s
Source_Title: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage Design Guide / CUDA Programming Guide — Unified and System Memory
Limitations: CPU/host buffering can hide short storage stalls, so use sustained/peak behavior rather than instantaneous equality only.

Rule_Name: Direct Storage-to-GPU Path Must Preserve Storage and PCIe/Interconnect Context
What_It_Means: When GPUDirect Storage or another direct path is used, storage performance must be evaluated together with the relevant path bandwidth and topology rather than treating storage throughput as isolated.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: storage BW; NIC/RAID BW; PCIe path; GPU destination
Output_Decision: Evaluate end-to-end path capacity and identify the limiting stage.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Direct storage-to-GPU path is enabled = Topology-dependent GB/s
Source_Title: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage Design Guide
Limitations: PCIe/network compatibility belongs to existing Compatibility Rules; this rule only evaluates storage-path resource demand.

Rule_Name: Storage Bottleneck Requires Evidence of Data-Starvation or I/O Wait
What_It_Means: Storage shall be classified as a bottleneck only when profiling/benchmark evidence links insufficient storage delivery or I/O wait to lost workload performance.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: storage throughput/IOPS/latency; GPU/CPU idle or wait time; target performance
Condition: Performance loss is attributable to storage
Output_Decision: Flag storage bottleneck and retain measured evidence.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Performance loss is attributable to storage = Evidence-based Boolean
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / GPUDirect Storage Benchmarking and Configuration Guide
Limitations: High utilization of storage alone does not prove application bottleneck; causal attribution is required.

Rule_Name: Single-Node Storage Must Be Sized Against Aggregate Node Demand
What_It_Means: For a single compute node, local/shared storage must sustain the aggregate storage demand generated by all relevant concurrent workloads on that node.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: per-process/per-GPU data demand; concurrent streams
Output_Decision: Size storage for aggregate measured/derived node demand.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Multiple processes share storage = Node-specific GB/s; IOPS
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / MLPerf Storage Working Group
Limitations: Do not multiply a benchmark result by GPU count unless per-accelerator demand and concurrency are comparable.

Rule_Name: Multi-Node Shared Storage Must Be Sized From Aggregate and Per-Node Demand
What_It_Means: Shared storage for multiple compute nodes shall be evaluated using aggregate offered load and per-node delivery requirements, preserving client count and workload context.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: nodes; per-node demand; aggregate demand; concurrency
Output_Decision: Evaluate both aggregate storage capacity/performance and per-node service.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Multiple nodes access common storage = Cluster/workload-derived GB/s; IOPS
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / MLPerf Storage Working Group
Limitations: MLPerf explicitly treats client-node count as workload/harness context; do not generalize per-node results.
Applicability: Shared filesystem/object storage for distributed AI workloads.
Example_or_Context: Shared filesystem/object storage for distributed AI workloads.

Rule_Name: Distributed Training Storage Must Preserve Access and Sharding Pattern
What_It_Means: For distributed training, storage sizing shall account for whether data is independently read from each node, shared, replicated, or sharded, because these patterns change aggregate storage traffic.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: data sharding; replication; nodes; local/shared storage; read pattern
Output_Decision: Produce storage demand for the actual distributed access pattern.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Distributed workload uses storage = Configuration-dependent GB/s; IOPS; TB
Source_Title: MLPerf Storage Benchmark v3.0 Results / MLPerf Storage v1.0 Benchmark Results / MLPerf Training Benchmark
Limitations: No universal linear scaling with node count; benchmark or trace the actual pattern.

Rule_Name: RAM Requirement Must Include All Concurrent Host-Side Components
What_It_Means: System RAM sizing shall be based on the sum of concurrently resident host-memory components required by the selected workload and software configuration, rather than dataset size or GPU count alone.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: dataset/staging; CPU model state; workers; prefetched batches; pinned buffers; cache; runtime; checkpoint staging; offloaded state
Condition: All listed components are concurrently resident or explicitly reserved
Output_Decision: Produce total required host-RAM estimate before applying WLR-MEM-01.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: All listed components are concurrently resident or explicitly reserved = Workload-derived GB
Source_Title: torch.utils.data — PyTorch main documentation / 2.6. Unified and System Memory — CUDA Programming Guide / Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel / CPU Offloading — Megatron Bridge / Cache management — Hugging Face Datasets
Limitations: Components must be de-duplicated; not every component is present in every workload.
Applicability: Training and inference workloads with any host-resident components.
Example_or_Context: Training and inference workloads with any host-resident components.

Rule_Name: System Memory Feasibility Reuses Existing WLR-MEM-01
What_It_Means: Candidate system RAM shall be accepted only when the calculated required system memory is within available system memory. This rule operationalizes the existing feasibility rule rather than duplicating it.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: Required_System_Memory; System_Memory_GB
Condition: Required system memory <= available system memory
Output_Decision: Pass RAM feasibility; otherwise reject/resize candidate.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Required system memory <= available system memory <= Workload-derived GB
Source_Title: MLPerf Training Benchmark
Limitations: Existing WLR-MEM-01 remains the canonical feasibility rule.

Rule_Name: Dataset Staging Memory Must Be Counted When Data Is Resident in RAM
What_It_Means: If a dataset, shard, decoded dataset portion, or staging buffer is intentionally resident in host RAM, that resident amount must be included in the RAM requirement.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: Resident dataset/shard size; staging-buffer size
Output_Decision: Add actual resident staging footprint to RAM estimate.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Host-resident staging is enabled = Measured/configured GB
Source_Title: Cache management — Hugging Face Datasets
Limitations: Dataset size on disk is not equivalent to RAM footprint; compression/decoding and representation can change memory use.
Applicability: Datasets using in-memory staging or explicit host staging.
Example_or_Context: Datasets using in-memory staging or explicit host staging.

Rule_Name: Preprocessing Working Memory Must Be Included
What_It_Means: CPU-side preprocessing that materializes intermediate arrays, decoded samples, transformed batches, or temporary representations must be included when those objects are resident in host RAM.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: Preprocessing intermediates; transform configuration; batch size
Output_Decision: Add peak concurrent preprocessing working set.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Preprocessing creates host-resident intermediates = Measured/derived GB
Source_Title: torch.utils.data — PyTorch main documentation / Main classes — Hugging Face Datasets
Limitations: No universal bytes-per-sample or percentage overhead is assumed.
Applicability: CPU preprocessing pipelines and dataset transformation workflows.
Example_or_Context: CPU preprocessing pipelines and dataset transformation workflows.

Rule_Name: DataLoader Worker Memory Must Scale With Worker Configuration
What_It_Means: RAM planning must account for memory consumed by data-loader worker processes and their dataset/process state when multi-process loading is enabled.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: num_workers; parent-process memory accessed by workers; worker state
Output_Decision: Increase host-RAM requirement according to measured/estimated worker footprint; do not use a universal worker-RAM constant.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: num_workers > 0 > 0 workers
Source_Title: torch.utils.data — PyTorch main documentation / Data Loading Optimization in PyTorch
Limitations: PyTorch explicitly warns that worker memory can approach parent-process memory for accessed Python objects; actual memory depends on dataset representation.

Rule_Name: Prefetched Batch Memory Must Be Included
What_It_Means: When data-loader workers prefetch batches, the memory footprint of prefetched batches must be included in host RAM planning.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: batch size; sample bytes; num_workers; prefetch_factor; number of concurrent queues
Output_Decision: Add peak prefetched-batch footprint.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Prefetching is enabled = Configured/Measured GB
Source_Title: Data Loading Optimization in PyTorch
Limitations: Prefetching behavior and representation can vary; formula is an upper-bound planning model, not a guaranteed allocation.

Rule_Name: Pinned Host Memory Must Be Included Separately
What_It_Means: If pin_memory/page-locked host buffers are enabled, their peak resident size must be included because pinned memory occupies host RAM and is used for CPU-GPU transfers.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: pinned buffer count; batch/buffer size; pin_memory configuration
Output_Decision: Reserve peak pinned host-memory footprint.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Pinned/page-locked buffers are used = Measured/configured GB
Source_Title: Data Loading Optimization in PyTorch / 2.6. Unified and System Memory — CUDA Programming Guide / CUDA Driver API — Host Memory Allocation
Limitations: NVIDIA warns that excessive page-locking can reduce memory available to the system; no universal pinned-memory fraction is assumed.
Applicability: Accelerator workloads using pinned host buffers.
Example_or_Context: Accelerator workloads using pinned host buffers.

Rule_Name: In-Memory Dataset Cache Is Optional and Must Be Explicit
What_It_Means: RAM planning shall include an in-memory dataset cache only when the workload/software configuration explicitly enables or requires keeping data in memory.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: keep_in_memory; configured RAM cache limit; cached dataset size
Output_Decision: Add configured/observed cache footprint; otherwise do not assume full-dataset caching.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: In-memory caching is enabled = Configured GB
Source_Title: Cache management — Hugging Face Datasets / Main classes — Hugging Face Datasets
Limitations: Cache behavior is library/configuration specific; disk cache does not imply equal RAM consumption.

Rule_Name: Dataset Cache and Dataset Staging Must Not Be Double Counted
What_It_Means: If the same dataset representation is already accounted for as an in-memory cache, it shall not be counted again as a separate staging component.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: cache footprint; staging footprint; object identity/representation
Condition: Two memory categories refer to the same resident representation
Output_Decision: Deduplicate memory components before total RAM calculation.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Two memory categories refer to the same resident representation = Overlap detected GB
Source_Title: Cache management — Hugging Face Datasets
Limitations: Requires component-level memory accounting.
Applicability: Any pipeline with caching and staging.
Example_or_Context: Any pipeline with caching and staging.

Rule_Name: CPU-Resident Model State Must Be Included
What_It_Means: Model parameters, gradients, optimizer state, master weights, or other model tensors resident in CPU RAM must be included when the training/inference configuration places them on the host.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: model parameter bytes; gradient bytes; optimizer bytes; CPU-offload settings
Condition: Any model-state component is resident in CPU RAM
Output_Decision: Add CPU-resident model-state footprint.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Any model-state component is resident in CPU RAM = Configured/Derived GB
Source_Title: CPU Offloading — Megatron Bridge
Limitations: Exact footprint depends on precision, optimizer, sharding and offload fraction; no universal multiplier is assumed.
Applicability: CPU optimizer/state/parameter offloading or CPU-resident model execution.
Example_or_Context: CPU optimizer/state/parameter offloading or CPU-resident model execution.

Rule_Name: Training RAM Must Include CPU-Offloaded Optimizer State When Enabled
What_It_Means: When optimizer CPU offloading is enabled, the selected offload fraction of optimizer state becomes a host-RAM requirement.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: optimizer-state size; optimizer_offload_fraction; distributed optimizer configuration
Output_Decision: Add the configured CPU-resident optimizer-state amount to RAM requirement.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: optimizer CPU offloading enabled > 0 fraction
Source_Title: CPU Offloading — Megatron Bridge
Limitations: Offload fraction is configuration-specific and does not imply a universal fraction.
Applicability: Training configurations using CPU optimizer offload.
Example_or_Context: Training configurations using CPU optimizer offload.

Rule_Name: CPU-Offloaded Activations Must Be Counted
What_It_Means: When activation CPU offloading is enabled, the host memory needed for the selected offloaded layers/activations must be included.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: activation footprint per layer; offloaded layer count; offload configuration
Output_Decision: Add peak CPU-resident activation footprint.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: CPU activation offloading enabled = Configured/Measured GB
Source_Title: CPU Offloading — Megatron Bridge / Performance Tuning Guide — NVIDIA NeMo Framework
Limitations: NVIDIA notes host-memory capacity can limit the number of layers that can be offloaded, especially when CPU memory is shared by multiple GPUs.

Rule_Name: Runtime/Framework Memory Must Be Included
What_It_Means: Host RAM used by the training/inference framework, runtime, process metadata, allocators, communication libraries, tokenizers, service logic, and other software-resident structures must be included when measured or explicitly configured.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: process RSS; framework allocations; runtime services; communication/shared-memory usage
Condition: Host runtime has non-zero resident memory beyond workload data/model components
Output_Decision: Add measured peak runtime footprint as a separate component.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Host runtime has non-zero resident memory beyond workload data/model components > 0 GB
Source_Title: torch.utils.data — PyTorch main documentation / Multiprocessing best practices / Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel
Limitations: Do not invent a percentage overhead; measure representative runs.

Rule_Name: Checkpoint Host-RAM Staging Must Be Counted When Used
What_It_Means: If the checkpoint implementation stages model/optimizer state through CPU memory before persistence, the peak staged amount must be included in host RAM planning.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: checkpoint state size; sharding; save mode; async checkpoint configuration
Condition: Checkpoint path copies/stages state through CPU memory
Output_Decision: Add peak checkpoint staging buffer to RAM requirement.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Checkpoint path copies/stages state through CPU memory = Configured/Measured GB
Source_Title: Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel / NeMo Distributed Checkpoint User Guide
Limitations: Sharded distributed checkpointing may avoid gathering the full state on one rank; do not assume full-checkpoint RAM unless the implementation requires it.
Applicability: Checkpoint implementations that use CPU staging or consolidation.
Example_or_Context: Checkpoint implementations that use CPU staging or consolidation.

Rule_Name: Inference Host RAM Must Reflect Serving-Side State
What_It_Means: Inference RAM planning must include host-resident model copies, tokenizer/runtime state, request queues, preprocessing buffers, cache and any explicitly configured CPU offload.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: model host copy; requests; queue buffers; preprocessing; cache; offload
Condition: Any listed serving component is resident in host RAM
Output_Decision: Produce inference-specific host RAM requirement.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Any listed serving component is resident in host RAM = Measured/configured GB
Source_Title: Checkpointing in NeMo Automodel / CPU Offloading — Megatron Bridge / Cache management — Hugging Face Datasets
Limitations: GPU KV-cache is not automatically a host-RAM component unless offloaded; avoid double counting.
Applicability: Online and batch inference where host-side serving state exists.
Example_or_Context: Online and batch inference where host-side serving state exists.

Rule_Name: Multi-GPU Host RAM Must Be Evaluated Per Host
What_It_Means: For a multi-GPU node, host RAM must be sufficient for the aggregate concurrent CPU-side state, worker processes, buffers and offloaded components associated with all GPUs/ranks on that host.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: GPU/rank count per host; per-rank CPU state; shared host state; worker/buffer memory
Condition: Multiple GPU/rank processes share one host
Output_Decision: Calculate peak host RAM from per-rank and shared components; do not use a universal RAM-to-GPU ratio.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Multiple GPU/rank processes share one host > 1 GPUs/host
Source_Title: Multiprocessing best practices / CPU Offloading — Megatron Bridge / Performance Tuning Guide — NVIDIA NeMo Framework
Limitations: Some memory is shared rather than replicated; actual process/sharing behavior must be measured or documented.

Rule_Name: Multi-Node RAM Must Be Sized Per Node
What_It_Means: For distributed multi-node workloads, RAM feasibility must be checked independently for every node configuration because dataset shard, rank, worker, cache and offload footprints can differ by node.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: nodes; GPUs/node; per-node dataset shard; per-node workers; per-node offload/cache
Output_Decision: Every node must satisfy its own RAM requirement; aggregate cluster RAM alone is insufficient.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Workload spans multiple nodes = Per-node GB/node
Source_Title: NeMo Distributed Checkpoint User Guide / Performance Tuning Guide — NVIDIA NeMo Framework / MLPerf Training Benchmark
Limitations: Requires explicit treatment of shared vs replicated state and data sharding.
Applicability: Distributed training/inference with potentially asymmetric node state.
Validation_Status: Derived DSS rule; supervisor/project approval required
Example_or_Context: Distributed training/inference with potentially asymmetric node state.

Rule_Name: Batch Size Can Increase Host RAM Through Data Pipeline Buffers
What_It_Means: Batch size shall be included in RAM modeling when it changes the size of resident batches, prefetched batches, preprocessing intermediates, request queues or pinned buffers.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: batch size; bytes/sample; workers; prefetch; preprocessing buffers
Condition: Batch size changes host-resident buffer sizes
Output_Decision: Recalculate host RAM for the selected batch size rather than treating RAM requirement as batch-independent.
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Batch size changes host-resident buffer sizes = Workload-dependent GB
Source_Title: Data Loading Optimization in PyTorch
Limitations: Relationship may be non-linear if batching changes representation or pipeline behavior.
Applicability: Training and batch/online inference pipelines with host-side batching.
Example_or_Context: Training and batch/online inference pipelines with host-side batching.

Rule_Name: CPU Workload Demand Must Be Characterized
What_It_Means: CPU sizing shall begin from CPU-side work actually performed by the workload, including orchestration, preprocessing, decoding, data movement and host-side computation.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: CPU work units; CPU time/unit; target workload rate; training/inference mode
Condition: CPU-side demand is characterized before CPU hardware selection
Output_Decision: Create workload-derived CPU demand input
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: CPU-side demand is characterized before CPU hardware selection = Workload-specific CPU-seconds/s
Source_Title: NVIDIA DALI Documentation / MLPerf Training Benchmark
Limitations: No universal GPU:CPU ratio, core threshold, thread multiplier or utilization threshold; requires measurement or comparable benchmark evidence.
Applicability: Workload-specific; apply only when referenced CPU stage is present.
Validation_Status: Research-supported; derived quantitative rules require project validation
Example_or_Context: Workload-specific; apply only when referenced CPU stage is present.

Rule_Name: CPU Capacity Must Meet Workload Demand
What_It_Means: Candidate CPU capacity shall be evaluated against measured or validated CPU-side workload demand at the target operating point.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: Required CPU throughput; candidate CPU throughput; target workload
Condition: Candidate CPU throughput >= required CPU throughput
Output_Decision: Pass CPU capacity or resize/optimize
What_Is_Checked_or_Calculated: Candidate CPU throughput >= required CPU throughput >= Workload-defined work units/s
Source_Title: MLPerf Training Benchmark / MLPerf Inference: Datacenter
Limitations: No universal GPU:CPU ratio, core threshold, thread multiplier or utilization threshold; requires measurement or comparable benchmark evidence.
Applicability: Workload-specific; apply only when referenced CPU stage is present.
Validation_Status: Research-supported; derived quantitative rules require project validation
Example_or_Context: Workload-specific; apply only when referenced CPU stage is present.

Rule_Name: CPU Core Requirement From Measured Service Demand
What_It_Means: CPU core demand should be derived from CPU service demand at the target workload rate rather than a fixed GPU-to-CPU ratio.
Why_It_Exists: Not separately documented in the source artifact.
Inputs: CPU time/workload unit; target workload rate
Condition: Equivalent CPU core demand is calculated from CPU-seconds consumed per second of target work
